answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce resource before it can submit trades or vote; the contract locks that bond and slashes it when a challenge proves the identity colluded or double-spent. A nebula of newly minted accounts therefore cannot gain influence for free: every fake identity needs its own capital, and coordinated attacks risk losing the full stake. Raising the bond on a glacier-like schedule as participation grows preserves access for honest newcomers while making the ridge of attack cost rise with the influence an attacker seeks.
